messages.author: 04e62c3b36bb17bf
messages.subject: Marker density problems
parts:
Hi Karl et al. 
This question may have been asked before... I am sure the problem plagues any of us using maps from NGS genotyping. 

I have a RAD genotyped population with ~4000 markers (its a BIG map w/ 2600 total cM). Many of these markers are in close proximity (as many as 8/cM).
To speed up QTL mapping, I have culled the map to include only a single marker / cM, and this works fine, but I am wondering if there is a better or more computationally efficient way to set up the map. What do you think about dropping all markers and using only the pseudomarkers for the analysis?

Any advice is appreciated!
John

John Lovell
Postdoc, UT Austin, USA.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Marker density problems
parts:
Hi, John,

I've run into the same issue; there's a function reduce2grid() for this.

data(hyper)
hyper <- calc.genoprob(hyper, step=2)
hypersub <- reduce2grid(hyper)
out <- scanone(hypersub)
plot(out, incl.markers=FALSE)

The only issue is that plots don't include the marker positions. :(

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Marker density problems
parts:
Thanks Karl. This works like a charm... No worries about the plots. 
Future reference, using reduce2grid allows us to run scanones in less than half of the time as the full cross object. 

> calc.test<-calc.genoprob(qtldata, step=2, stepwidth="fixed", error.prob=0.0001)
> system.time(plot(scanone(calc.test, pheno.col=2, method="hk")))
   user  system elapsed 
 12.747   5.850  18.611 
> calc.sub <- reduce2grid(calc.test)
> system.time(plot(scanone(calc.sub, pheno.col=2, method="hk")))
   user  system elapsed 
  4.631   2.490   7.124

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Marker density problems
parts:
The new function, scantwopermhk, works, at least if you use assumeCondIndep=TRUE:

data(hyper)
hyper <- calc.genoprob(hyper, step=2.5)
hyper <- reduce2grid(hyper)
out <- scantwopermhk(hyper, assumeCondIndep=TRUE, n.perm=16)

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Marker density problems
parts:
You might also consider the pickMarkerSubset function, which seeks to select a subset of markers with no two markers closer than d cM apart. (But it's not very easy to use.)

Related to this paper: Broman, K. W. and Weber, J. L. (1999) Method for constructing confidently ordered linkage maps.Genet. Epidemiol., 16, 337–343. https://www.biostat.wisc.edu/~kbroman/publications/framework.pdf

karl
